title: Indian Railways in 5 Numbers
sources: Vivek Express, Dibrugarh to Kanyakumari: India's longest train route, about 4,150-4,190 km (Indian Railways / Northeast Frontier Railway timetable)
Gorakhpur Junction platform: about 1.37 km after the 2013 remodelling, among the longest railway platforms in the world (Ministry of Railways)
Chenab Bridge, Jammu and Kashmir: 359 m above the river bed, the world's highest railway arch bridge (Ministry of Railways, opened 2025)
Indian Railways employs about 1.2 million people (Ministry of Railways annual statistics)
Indian Railways carries close to 2 crore passengers a day (about 673 crore passenger journeys in 2023-24, Ministry of Railways)

lines.text: Number five: the Vivek Express runs more than four thousand kilometres, from Dibrugarh to Kanyakumari.
Number four: the platform at Gorakhpur is about one point three kilometres long.
Number three: the Chenab bridge stands three hundred and fifty nine metres above the river.
lines.caps: THE *CHENAB BRIDGE | *359 METRES | ABOVE THE RIVER

lines.text: Number two: the railways employ about one point two million people.
And number one: close to two crore passengers ride every single day.
Which one surprised you? Comment one to five.
